column1: # The fourth column is required for the avif channel: the normalised first line of the Rust text (ok, no-gainmap; see norm_avif in run.sh). The line covers only that outcome; a dropped gain map (dropped), a read error (rust-<class>) or any other outcome is a difference.
# Documented, expected deviations only: a difference nobody understands is a bug, not a line here.

# The decoded planes have the channels heifpix-base, heifpix-gm, avifpix-base and avifpix-gm (each with -info and -yuv). A line for "avifpix-gm" covers avifpix-gm-info and avifpix-gm-yuv, and nothing else; the bare "heifpix" or "avifpix" would also hide the base image, so it is not used. A file that libavif ignores the gain map of has no libavif gain-map planes, so the Rust gain-map planes of it are not compared with any oracle (see docs/parity.md).

# channel: uhdr (every uhdr-* channel: txt, dims, base-jpg, gm-jpg, base-rgba, gm-raw), uhdr-txt (one of them), avif, xmp, turbo-base-rgba, turbo-gm-raw, exiftool-mpimage2 (a prefix such as "turbo" or "exiftool" covers all its channels).

# A JPEG that libultrahdr cannot read is gated by turbo-base-rgba, turbo-gm-raw, exiftool-mpimage2 and the xmp channel, and run.sh reports a missing Rust gain map for it as a difference (turbo-* missing-rust) that a uhdr line cannot hide (a turbo or turbo-* line would); an AVIF is gated by the avif channel, and a known line there hides only the Rust outcome in its fourth column.
